data.text:
RALLY FATIGUE NA?

Former Eastern Samar governor Ben Evardone believes the public may be experiencing rally fatigue as several key suspects in the corruption scandal remain at large.

"Kung hindi maraming dumalo sa Luneta at saka dito sa EDSA, sa People Power Monument, baka nagkaroon ng rally fatigue na ’yung mga tao at saka sabihin, wala namang nangyayari, rally tayo nang rally," said Evardone.

He also noted that the timing of the anti-corruption rallies may be off, as most Filipinos are already in a “Christmas mood.”

"Actually, Christmas mood na tayo lahat eh. And may mga Christmas parties na rin eh. So ito, parang sa timing, parang nawawala na," he added.

‘PNP, PROTEKTOR NG CORRUPT’ 

Sa kainitan ng pagmamartsa ng mga rallyista patungong Mendiola, Maynila, ngayong Linggo, Nobyembre 30 hinarangan ng pulisya ang mga kalahok sa Baha sa Luneta 2.0 mass action sa Recto Avenue, Maynila gamit ang mga konkretong barikada, razor wired fence, at container van. 
 
Maririnig naman ang pagsigaw ng mga rallyista ng “PNP, protektor ng korap,” habang sinasabayan ito ng hanay ng kapulisan sa pagkalampag ng kanilang riot shields bilang panakot sa mga demonstrador. 

(Video credits: Altermidya/Facebook)

data.text:
More than 16,000 police officers were placed on standby across Metro Manila on Sunday, November 30 as anti-corruption demonstrations Day drew just over 7,000 protesters. 

Crowd estimates showed around 3,000 participants in Luneta and about 4,500 along EDSA—far smaller than the Sept. 21 rallies, which gathered 70,000 in Luneta and 49,000 on EDSA. 

On Saturday, NCRPO spokesperson Police Major Hazel Asilo said in a radio interview that 16,670 personnel had been readied for deployment to secure all monitored sites. 

She added that the police force was “all systems go” for crowd control, traffic management, and maintaining public order throughout the day.
